title: Callback Refs and Measuring the DOM
summary: Connect a React element to browser measurement tools without querying the page globally.
nestedConcepts: Use effects for setup and cleanup

subtopics.title: Receive the DOM node
subtopics.explanation: React calls a callback ref with the attached DOM element. When that element is removed, React signals that it is no longer attached. This lets a component set up work at the right moment. It is like receiving a key only when a room is ready to use.

subtopics.title: Measure a current layout
subtopics.explanation: `getBoundingClientRect()` returns the element’s current size and position. The result can become outdated after content, fonts, or viewport changes. Do not measure during render; update after the browser has laid out the page. A ruler gives one measurement, not a promise about tomorrow.

subtopics.title: Observe future changes
subtopics.explanation: ResizeObserver reports when an element’s size changes. Attach it when the node is available and disconnect it when the node is removed. This is more reliable than repeatedly checking dimensions on a timer. It is like a door sensor that signals when the room changes.

subtopics.title: Use effects for setup and cleanup
subtopics.explanation: An effect can attach an observer or browser listener after rendering and clean it up when dependencies change or the component unmounts. Keep the observer instance associated with the element it watches. Cleanup prevents stale callbacks from updating a page that no longer exists.

subtopics.title: Prefer CSS when possible
subtopics.explanation: Container queries and intrinsic layout often solve responsive sizing without JavaScript. Measure only when the value drives behavior, such as sizing a canvas drawing surface. Fewer DOM reads make the component simpler and reduce forced layout work.

foundations.overview: A callback ref is a function React calls when it attaches or detaches a DOM element. It helps connect a component to browser tools such as ResizeObserver. Use measurement only when layout information changes behavior. A measurement is a snapshot, so observe changes and clean up the observer.
foundations.mentalModel: A callback ref is a delivery notice: React tells you when the element has arrived and when it leaves.
foundations.whyItMatters: Some browser capabilities need a real DOM element, such as focusing an input or measuring a panel.
foundations.formalDefinition: A callback ref is a function that receives a DOM node when React attaches it and receives null when React detaches it.
foundations.browserPerspective: The browser reports element dimensions through layout APIs and ResizeObserver; React controls when the element is attached.
foundations.realWorldUsage: Use a ref for focus, canvas integration, intersection observation, or layout measurement that cannot be solved with CSS.
foundations.businessImpact: Correct measurement supports stable charts, responsive widgets, and reliable keyboard focus.
foundations.engineeringImpact: Keep DOM work local to the component and disconnect observers during cleanup.
foundations.performanceImpact: Avoid reading layout repeatedly during rendering; observe changes and batch visual updates.
commonUseCases: Focus an input after opening a dialog
Resize a chart to its container
Start observation when a component mounts
commonMisconceptions: Refs trigger rerenders when they change
Changing a ref value does not trigger a React render.
Layout can change after fonts, content, or viewport dimensions change.
A callback ref is the same as a click callback
React calls it when the DOM attachment changes, not after a user action.

keyTakeaways: React calls a callback ref with the attached DOM element.
`getBoundingClientRect()` returns the element’s current size and position.
ResizeObserver reports when an element’s size changes.

codeLab.title: Measure an element with a callback ref
codeLab.instructions: Show the rendered width of a panel. Attach a callback ref and use ResizeObserver to update the width when the panel changes size.
codeLab.expectedOutput: The displayed width updates after the panel or viewport changes size.
hints: Break the task into state, event handling, and rendered feedback.
Keep the interface accessible with labels and meaningful button text.
